_what_this_is: The test suites known to be RED, so a genuinely new regression can be told from the existing set. Read by tools/known_red_check.py. REPORT ONLY.
_how_it_was_measured: python tools/run_all_tests.py in a DETACHED GIT WORKTREE at origin/main, isolated from every working-tree change in this clone. 396 files ran, 0 skipped, and the runner reported the tree was NOT dirtied -- so no row here is a cascade from a probe that left a file modified, which is the failure that has made this measurement wrong before. DIAGNOSES added 2026-09-16 by running each suite ALONE in a detached worktree at origin/main and reading the failing arm -- never from the runner's one-line tail, which names the arm and not the cause.
_what_an_empty_why_means: NOT DIAGNOSED YET, recorded as empty rather than guessed. An invented cause is worse than a blank one because it ends the investigation. tools/known_red_check.py reports how many entries are undiagnosed, so a blank is a backlog rather than a shrug.
_what_this_is_NOT: Not an allow-list and not a gate. An entry does not make a failure acceptable -- it makes it ATTRIBUTABLE. An entry whose suite has gone GREEN is reported as RECOVERED and must be deleted: while it stands it swallows the next real failure of that file.

entries.why: GREEN IN ISOLATION, RED UNDER FULL-SUITE LOAD. Measured 2026-09-16: exit 0 when run alone in a clean worktree at origin/main, red in the 396-file run. This is the concurrency shape run_all_tests.py already names and carries a retry set for (CONCURRENCY_SENSITIVE), and these files are not in it. NOT KNOWN TO BE A BROKEN SUITE -- and equally not known to be sound, because a suite that only fails under load may be failing for a real reason that only load exposes. The next step is to establish which, not to add it to the retry set.

The arm "EVERY registered resource is read -- derived from the registry, not retyped" fails: the SAIRNlaw resource registry has gained resources the hydrate path does not read. The arm is derived rather than hardcoded, which is why it noticed; a retyped list would have stayed green and been wrong.

entries.tail: 4b  and it says WHY -- a restore cannot be verified against a modified baseline
entries.why: Arms 4a and 4b: "a dirty tree exits 2, not 0 or 1" got exit 1. The tool is meant to report COULD-NOT-RUN when the tree is modified, because a restore cannot be verified against a moving baseline, and it is returning a finding instead. A third state collapsing into a verdict -- the exact shape PR 1.11 names.

entries.tail: ok   layer has a population of exactly three
entries.why: The arm "every dimension is present" fails. The dispersion report is expected to carry every dimension it declares and one is absent. Not traced further than the arm; the dimension that went missing is the next thing to establish.

entries.tail: 7e  CONTROL: the same rows marked OPEN pass -- 7d is not a checker that refuses everything
entries.why: Arm 7e reports NO BASELINE: the SPOF register fixture "has no BASELINE: N components at or above line. Without a frozen denominator a register that shrank by four and one that never moved print the same number." The probe is refusing to score against an unfrozen denominator, which is correct behaviour -- the fixture or the register needs the baseline line.

entries.tail: - NO RECORDED INSPECTION is stale, incomplete, or cites an arm that does not exist -- the half this probe controls
entries.why: The arm "NO RECORDED INSPECTION is stale, incomplete, or cites an arm that does not exist". Two records have drifted hashes: Hank's inspections of tools/dispatch_state.py and tools/retry_backoff_check.py, both of which were edited after being inspected. Deliberately NOT fixed by re-hashing -- re-hashing somebody else's inspection without re-inspecting would launder a stale record into a fresh-looking one. It needs those two artefacts re-inspected by a session that is not their author.

entries.tail: 3b  1.7   fires on 43% of the tree (must be under 35%)
entries.why: Arm 3b: standing rule 1.7 fires on 43% of the tree and the criterion is under 35%. A calibration failure rather than a broken probe: the rule is matching too much of the platform to be evidence of anything. Either the rule needs narrowing or the threshold was set against a smaller tree.

entries.tail: --- C. an invisible character inside a real regex ---
entries.why: A STALE ANCHOR, and its own guard is what reports it: "AssertionError: the SABOTAGE did not land: anchor no longer in api/_lib/accounting-connector.js -- '/^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$/'". The date regex it plants into is gone from that file. This is the guarded failure mode working exactly as designed -- it refuses rather than running the checker against an unmodified file and reporting a pass. The fix is a new anchor, not a new guard.

entries.tail: ooda_phases.py                         exit 2 (the tool could not tell):   ARMS FAILED
entries.why: ooda_phases.py --selftest exits 2 (the tool could not tell), which this probe correctly refuses to fold into a pass. THE DEFECT IS IN ooda_phases.py, NOT IN THE PROBE, and tests/run_selftest_sweep_probe.py is red on the same underlying fact -- so these two entries are ONE defect seen from two places. Fixing ooda_phases.py should clear both, and if it clears only one that is itself a finding.

Arm C2, "and lists them". Confirmed red at origin/main on 2026-09-16 by the same method: a local branch reported 34 checks 1 failed against 32 checks 1 failed at origin, i.e. the same single failure with two arms added beside it.

The arm "the real SAIRN tree currently has no UNBASELINED occurrence" expects 0 and finds more. A NEW occurrence of the truthy-sum shape has appeared somewhere and is not in the baseline. This is the one entry in this registry most likely to be a REAL CURRENT DEFECT in product code rather than test drift, and it should be read before the others.

entries.tail: FAILED TWICE, the second time on its own: CHECK 4 VERIFIED (planted blocks by seam + names the field, clean not blocked by seam): False
entries.why: SHARED CAUSE D -- this probe drives a REAL push and the verdict it reads is the one the whole gate stack returns, not the one check 4 returns. It now reports "CHECK 4 VERIFIED ...: False" because an EARLIER gate refuses the push first, so check 4 never gets to answer. Same root as check7_probe and check8_probe, whose failures carry `rejected_by_remote` and "failed to push some refs" outright. The gate stack grew (register-feed, generated-docs) and these three probes assume they are the first refusal.
